geological_context: Gale Crater is a 154-km-diameter impact basin formed ~3.8 to 3.5 billion years ago (late Noachian to early Hesperian). At its center lies Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), a 5.5-km-tall mound of layered sedimentary deposits preserving billions of years of Martian climate and hydrological history.

target_features.boxwork_ridges: Three-dimensional networks of intersecting polygonal mineralized veins protruding 1 to 5 meters in relief above surrounding eroded mudstone bedrock.
target_features.sulfate_clay_transition: A prominent geochemical boundary recording the planetary transition from a wetter, neutral-pH lacustrine environment (clay-rich smectites) to an evaporating hyper-saline arid climate (polyhydrated magnesium sulfates).
target_features.yardangs_and_dunes: Wind-sculpted yardangs and localized transverse aeolian sand ridges (TARs) occupying valleys between resistant caprock layers.

instruments.hirise: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (MRO): 0.25 to 0.3 m/pixel optical resolution.
instruments.mola: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MGS): Topographical datum reference and regional elevation.
instruments.hrsc: High Resolution Stereo Camera (Mars Express): Digital terrain models and slope gradient derivation.
instruments.themis: Thermal Emission Imaging System (Mars Odyssey): Nighttime thermal inertia (duricrust vs loose dust). Caveat: Not a live weather forecast.
instruments.crism: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (MRO): Hyperspectral absorption bands for hydrated minerals.
instruments.rad: Radiation Assessment Detector (MSL / Curiosity): Surface galactic cosmic ray dose rates (~25 μSv/hr nominal baseline). Caveat: Historical record does not establish future human exposure.
